name: Neko no Naku Koro ni
source:
“Himuro Mountain, January 1970”

-Come on, hold on, everything will be all right, push, push!

Some say that in this world, everything is connected and everything has it's reason. A butterfly can move his wings in the Amazonas and its effect can be seen on the other side of the world.

-I can see her head, Oh, my lord, it's...! Keep pushing, darling!

But, how many flaps does it take to unleash a tragedy?

-Only a bit more...

How many tragedies does it take to erase it? Maybe the answer is easier than you may think.

In an isolated mountain, in the middle of a brutal snowstorm, a baby cries. Right away, the cats cry. When cats cry, blood flows then, and the flesh exists no more.

[Shortened from [url=http://lemmasoft.renai.us/forums/viewtopic.php?f=11&t=8751]Lemma Soft Forums[/url]]
translation:
“冰室山，1970年1月”

——加油，坚持住，一切都会没事的，用力，再用力！

有人说，这个世界上的一切都彼此相连，凡事皆有其原因。亚马孙的一只蝴蝶扇动翅膀，其影响可能会出现在世界另一端。

——我看见她的头了。天啊，那是…！继续用力，亲爱的！

可是，究竟要扇动多少次翅膀，才能引发一场悲剧？

——只差一点了…

又需要多少场悲剧，才能将它抹去？答案或许比你想象的更简单。

在一座与世隔绝的山中，一场残酷的暴风雪中央，婴儿发出了啼哭。紧接着，猫也开始鸣叫。猫哭之时，鲜血流淌，血肉不复存在。

[精简自[url=http://lemmasoft.renai.us/forums/viewtopic.php?f=11&t=8751]Lemma Soft Forums[/url]]
